clue.text: British PM's keeping payment back for election transport

indicators.note: keeping says the possessive name holds the reversed payment inside it

parts.note: Clement Attlee was the post-war Labour Prime Minister, so the possessive gives Attlee's

indicators.note: back says the word for payment is read from right to left

parts.note: a sub is a subscription payment, or an advance on wages

explanation.surface: A prime minister holds back some money meant for the coaches that ferry a campaign around.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement Attlee was Britain's post-war Labour Prime Minister; 'back' reverses the payment and 'keeping' puts it inside his possessive name.
explanation.definitionFit: Campaign coaches carrying candidates and their teams around the country are known by this name during elections.

clue.text: Rock climbing is great

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Rock is the nickname of Gibraltar, shortened to Gib

explanation.surface: A climber praises rock climbing as wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: Gibraltar is known as 'the Rock' and abbreviated Gib; 'climbing' reverses it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Large and great are simple synonyms, as in a great big dog or a great house.

clue.text: Tourist getting rid of pennies, one hears

definitions.note: one who hears a case, as a judge does

indicators.note: getting rid of says some letters are taken out of the tourist word

parts.note: a tripper is a day tourist
P is the abbreviation for penny, so PP is pennies

explanation.surface: A sightseer spends their coppers, and someone overhears it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one hears' looks like a sound-alike signal, but it is the definition: a person who hears and decides a case.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, a person or body that tries a case, hearing the evidence and deciding it, is so called.

clue.text: Trouble about beginning of month: uprising in Baltic province

indicators.note: in a down entry uprising means the whole is read from bottom to top
about says the trouble word goes round the date

parts.note: to ail is to trouble
Nov 1, the first of November, is the beginning of that month

explanation.surface: Unrest early in the month leads to a revolt in a Baltic territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning of month' is a date, NOV I (1 November); 'about' wraps AIL round it and 'uprising' reverses AINOVIL in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic region on the Baltic coast, now divided between Latvia and Estonia, once a province of the Russian Empire.

clue.text: Cake from French fellow alone contributing to his neighbour's diet?

definitions.note: his refers back to the French fellow; the parliament of his neighbour across the Rhine

parts.note: a bun is a small cake
de is French for from
a stag is a man attending a social event without a female partner

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's pastry is mocked as part of what a German would eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diet' looks like food but is a legislative assembly; the French fellow's neighbour is Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Germany's federal parliament is traditionally called a diet, an old word for a legislative assembly.

clue.text: One way to cook casserole wife's missed before noon

indicators.note: missed says the letter for wife is dropped from the dish

parts.note: a casserole is a stew
a.m. means ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: A cook ruefully notes that the morning's casserole was left uneaten by his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooking food over boiling water's vapour is one standard method, alongside boiling and frying.

clue.text: Grotty pub opening bottles? That's another story

indicators.note: bottles means contains, so the opening holds the mixed letters

parts.note: a slot is an opening

indicators.note: grotty means shabby and run-down, so the letters of pub are in a mess

explanation.surface: A shabby bar opens its bottles, and the speaker says that's a separate tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottles' looks like the drink but works as a verb meaning holds: SLOT holds UBP, the mixed letters of pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondary storyline running alongside the main plot of a novel or play is literally another story.

clue.text: You'll need a hand, cutting fruit in half

indicators.note: in half says only the first half of the fruit's name is kept

parts.note: a pawpaw is a tropical fruit, the papaya

explanation.surface: Someone cutting fruit in two will need help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' joins; 'in half' keeps the front half of PAWPAW.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's foot, and informally a human hand, as in keep your mitts or paws off.

clue.text: Scout hit by heavy wave

parts.note: to pat is to hit lightly
a roller is a long heavy sea wave

explanation.surface: A Boy Scout is knocked over by a big wave at the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scout' looks like a youth movement member, but it means one who reconnoitres.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who goes on a patrol, reconnoitring an area, is acting as a scout.

clue.text: Properly handled, we learners got on under staff supervision

indicators.note: in a down entry under puts the second piece below the first

parts.note: L is a learner, from the learner plate, so LL is learners
to man is to staff
got on means grew older, aged

explanation.surface: We trainees did well because staff were keeping an eye on us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' places AGED below MAN in this down answer; 'supervision' completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Something run efficiently and with skill is said to be organised and handled well.

clue.text: Note Welshman's tucked into basmati and beef?

definitions.note: beef as slang for a complaint

parts.note: G is a musical note

indicators.note: tucked into says the name goes inside the grain

parts.note: basmati is a variety of rice
Evan is a typically Welsh man's name

explanation.surface: A dinner of rice and beef is served up with a Welshman's name in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' looks like the meat to go with the rice, but it is slang for a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef is informal for a complaint or grudge, which is just what a grievance is.

clue.text: In retrospect, chalet obviously offers sleeping accommodation

indicators.note: retrospect, looking back, says the hidden letters are read backwards
In says the letters sit inside the words chalet obviously

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Looking back, the chalet was plainly a place to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave 'In retrospect' wholly to the reversal; 'In' is better read as the hidden-word signal, with 'retrospect' alone turning LETOB around.
explanation.definitionFit: A moored boat run as a hotel provides beds for guests, so it offers sleeping accommodation.

clue.text: Estuary eroding rocks

indicators.note: rocks as a verb means shakes up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An estuary is wearing away the rocks along its shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' looks like a noun for the stones being worn away, but it is a verb signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The French tidal inlet near Bordeaux, where the Garonne and Dordogne meet, is a well-known estuary.

clue.text: Fail to visit Chinese tourist attraction

parts.note: to go to a place is to visit it
the Great Wall of China, known simply as the Wall

explanation.surface: Someone misses seeing the Great Wall on their trip to China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fail to visit' reads as missing the sight, but 'Fail' alone is the definition and 'to' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be ruined or go bankrupt, as a collapsing business does.

clue.text: Chap's business in shopping arcade taking millions

indicators.note: in says the business goes inside the arcade

parts.note: a mall is a shopping arcade
CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A man's company in a shopping centre is earning millions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chap' here is any man's name; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A common male first name, so it can stand for a chap, any man.

clue.text: Crime force has ignored by a character from Athens

indicators.note: has ignored says the letter for force is left out of the crime

parts.note: theft is a crime
F is the physics abbreviation for force

explanation.surface: A police force has overlooked a crime committed by someone from Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'force' sounds like the police but is the physics symbol F; 'character' is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter of the Greek alphabet, the eighth, written in Athens and elsewhere in Greece.

clue.text: Newspaper chief squeezed out

parts.note: the Express is a British national daily newspaper
ED, editor, is the chief of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper's editor has been forced out of the job.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Express is a British newspaper; ED for editor fits the newspaper surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Juice pressed from fruit is said to be extracted this way, the literal sense of pressing out.

clue.text: Test cricket side welcomes extremely tough competition

indicators.note: welcomes says the test takes in the outer letters

parts.note: a trial is a test

indicators.note: extremely says to take the very ends of the word tough

parts.note: the on side is one half of a cricket field, also called leg

explanation.surface: A cricket team in a Test match faces very hard opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Test cricket side' reads as a national team, but splits into two pieces; the on side is the leg half of a cricket field.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporting event of swimming, cycling and running in sequence, a multi-sport race.

clue.text: Plotter in capital city surrounded by explosive

indicators.note: surrounded by says the city sits inside the explosive

parts.note: TNT is an explosive
Riga is the capital of Latvia

explanation.surface: A conspirator in a capital is hemmed in by bombs.
explanation.definitionFit: A schemer who engages in secret intrigue is a plotter; the word is borrowed from French.

clue.text: Champion returned prize following match?

indicators.note: returned says the prize word is read backwards

parts.note: a pot is a prize, a trophy cup
a match gives a light

explanation.surface: A champion hands back the trophy after the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' suggests the sporting contest, but it is a match struck for a light.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means excellent, of the highest class, which a champion performer is.

clue.text: Pressurises poor kid

parts.note: lean means meagre, poor, as in lean times
a son is a kid

explanation.surface: Someone puts pressure on a hard-up child.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to put pressure on someone to get them to do something.

clue.text: Ultimate in incentives for good child

indicators.note: ultimate in means the final letter of the next word

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: The last word in rewards for a well-behaved child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is not a link here; it is PRO, as in pros and cons.
explanation.definitionFit: A British slang word for a child, a youngster or kid.

clue.text: English teacher and students turning up so early in the day?

definitions.note: a phrase for a time of day standing for a noun naming that moment

indicators.note: in a down entry turning up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: sir is how British pupils address a male teacher
NUS is the National Union of Students, a British students' body

explanation.surface: An English teacher and his pupils arrive remarkably early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' looks like arriving, but reverses E SIR NUS. NUS is Britain's National Union of Students.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn, when the sun appears, is a time very early in the day.

clue.text: Fashionable, say, wearing flowing mantle cut away at the front

indicators.note: wearing says the cloak goes round the example
flowing means the cloak's letters move freely into a new order
cut away at the front says the opening letter of mantle is removed

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means here

explanation.surface: Fashion, for instance, means wearing a flowing cloak trimmed at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut away at the front' drops M to leave ANTLE; 'flowing' mixes it to ELANT; 'wearing' puts EG inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Stylish and graceful in dress and manner, as a fashionable person aims to be.

clue.text: Floor cover

definitions.meaning: to floor is to baffle or disconcert someone
a light blanket or rug draped over a sofa or bed

explanation.definitionFit: To disconcert someone is to floor them; and a light blanket over furniture is a cover.

clue.text: Set fire to coal, left out by daughter

indicators.note: by places the daughter beside the shortened coal
out says the letter for left is removed from the coal

parts.note: lignite is soft brown coal

explanation.surface: A daughter lit the coal that had been left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' reads as one phrase, but splits: L for left, and 'out' removing it.
explanation.definitionFit: To kindle or light something is to make it burn, to start a fire.

clue.text: Colour to conceal a blemish

indicators.note: to conceal says the colour hides the article inside it

parts.note: a tint is a colour

explanation.surface: Some tinted cosmetic is used to hide a spot on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A stain or flaw, a mark that spoils something's purity, as in a moral or physical blemish.

clue.text: I pass out in part of church

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Someone faints in a part of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass out' reads as fainting, but 'out' is the signal to rearrange I PASS.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant name for the apse, the rounded recess at a church's east end.

clue.text: Discovering director at last is entering film studios

indicators.note: at last means the final letter of director
entering says the word is goes into the studios

parts.note: Ealing Studios is a famous film studio in west London

explanation.surface: A director finally gets into the film studios.
explanation.walkthrough: Ealing Studios in west London made the classic Ealing comedies.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming to understand or finding something out is a kind of discovering.

clue.text: I'm surprised American regularly goes east

indicators.note: regularly says to take every other letter of goes

explanation.surface: Someone is surprised that the American often heads east.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild exclamation of surprise or enthusiasm, chiefly heard in the United States.

clue.text: Upper crust headgear?

definitions.meaning: the pastry top covering a pie
slang for a hat or helmet

explanation.surface: Posh people's hats.
explanation.definitionFit: A pie's top pastry crust covers it; and a hat is slang for what goes on the head.

clue.text: Heaters went bust in old cinema

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: The heating broke down in an old picture house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' looks like the heaters breaking, but it rearranges the letters of heaters went.
explanation.definitionFit: Old cinemas that showed newsreels and short films continuously were given this name.
